neighbours.label: The word ' up' right after 'wake' ('wake up'), and 'Awakening' as a name
fire: Many people wake up at three in the morning with new worries about the day ahead.
Every day I wake up and thank the Lord that I was born in this valley.
The product is called Rise-N-Shine Wake Up On Time and it sold well last winter.
She set three alarms so that she would wake up before the sun.
There is a Healing Awakening meeting at the church hall on the nineteenth of May.
The children wake up early on Saturdays and run straight to the kitchen.
Wake up and smell the coffee, said the sign over the door of the little cafe.
He could not wake up properly until he had splashed cold water on his face.
quiet: Many people get up at three in the morning with new worries about the day ahead.
Every day I wake and thank the Lord that I was born in this valley.
The product is called Rise-N-Shine Clock On Time and it sold well last winter.
She set three alarms so that she would stand up before the sun.
There is a Healing Prayer meeting at the church hall on the nineteenth of May.
The children sit up late on Saturdays and run straight to the kitchen.
Look up and smell the coffee, said the sign over the door of the little cafe.
He could not sleep properly until he had splashed cold water on his face.

notes: Weak pole (max 1.09), broad. Near misses use other phrasal verbs and 'wake' without 'up'.
